summary: Four-legged steel lookout, about 100 ft, on Little Black Mountain near Evarts, KY; described by a 1950 federal survey and listed standing on 2023 imagery.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with a square lookout cab on top, painted grey

access.note: The 1950 survey route ran along a gravel road into mine company land, through a locked gate. No source says whether the gate is still locked or whether the public may go up.

events.note: Harlan Daily Enterprise item proposing a 100-foot steel lookout on Little Black Mountain; a proposal, not a completed tower
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: a standing four-legged steel tower with a square lookout cab; station first observed 1950
Forest Lookouts lists the tower as standing per Google Earth imagery dated 4/4/2023

notes_for_editor: Build date not found: the 1936 item is a proposal and the first description of a standing tower is from 1950. Record coordinates (36.8226, -83.1488) agree with the NGS position (36 49 21.27 N, 83 08 55.55 W). Forest Lookouts' Kentucky index also lists a separate 'BERCKMANN (PUTNEY)' entry for Harlan County; the Berckmann page itself describes the Little Black station, so check whether the name is shared with the Putney tower on Pine Mountain. Origin of the name Berckmann is not explained in sources read. Access is a 1950 route through mine land; verify before any visit. Record agency field holds the status line (see corrections).
